final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition with a 150 billion CHF Confederation indemnification cap (UBS absorbs first 50B), AT1 subordination locked in the deed, deposit guarantee filed by 18:30, and announcement at 19:30 Friday night with signed documents. SNB provides unlimited emergency liquidity; Federal Council commits to three-day draw speed on audited losses.
minority_objections: SNB warned that absence of institutional exit instructions is not confirmation of stability—clients are waiting for Monday open
AT1_rep repeatedly pressed that the rescue structure depends on Monday not opening into panic, calling it 'a prayer not a legal defense'
Wealth_client warned that if institutional clients (400M sitting flat) can walk at Monday open, the stabilization is an illusion
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs UBS on loss ceiling: UBS demanded Confederation backstop above 50B or would walk; resolved at 150B total cap
FINMA vs room on timeline: FINMA drew hard line that no announcement happens until documents legally filed by 18:30, forcing Friday night signatures
SNB vs Federal Council on facility costs: SNB insisted facility costs sit outside 150B cap but warned of political exposure if it becomes primary funding
AT1_rep vs FINMA on subordination language: fought over whether AT1 absorbs losses *before* Confederation draw triggers or is merely *junior to* it
key_concessions: Federal Council raised cap from 100B to 150B to secure UBS signature
UBS accepted 50B first-loss position in exchange for 150B hard ceiling with zero reopener
FINMA agreed to file deposit guarantee and AT1 schedule by 18:30 to enable Friday 19:30 announcement instead of Sunday
SNB accepted that facility costs sit outside 150B cap but secured three-day draw commitment to limit exposure
Room accepted that 400M institutional deposits are not contractually locked and may flee Monday morning
red_lines: UBS: will not sign without 150B Confederation cap as hard ceiling with zero reopener language in deed itself
FINMA: no announcement until deposit guarantee and indemnification schedule legally filed and signed
Federal Council: will not put Confederation name on unsigned commitments or announce before documents locked
SNB: three-day draw speed on audited losses or facility becomes primary funding and politically untenable
AT1_rep: subordination must be sequenced as 'AT1 absorbs losses first before any draw' not 'AT1 junior to draw'
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Institutional deposits (400M) are not contractually locked and can flee at Monday open—room acknowledged this but proceeded anyway
Deposit stabilization (2.3B inflows) is 70% wealth clients; institutional flat—room noted this but treated Friday night announcement as sufficient
Real test is Monday morning market open, not Friday night flows—multiple speakers warned this but no contingency plan beyond Sunday 06:00 bridge call
If Monday opens weak, inherited panic becomes 'existential' per UBS—acknowledged but not addressed with binding commitments
downstream_risk_variables: Monday market open reaction: if weak, institutional 400M flees and wealth clients may reverse
Litigation risk on AT1 subordination language despite FINMA assurances it holds in court
SNB facility becoming primary funding if Confederation draw is delayed beyond three days
Parliamentary backlash if 150B cap is breached or if SNB facility costs spiral
UBS walking post-announcement if due diligence surfaces liabilities beyond 150B cap
uncertainty_notes: Room locked Friday 19:30 announcement with signed documents to prevent weekend panic, but acknowledged the real test is Monday morning market open. Institutional deposits (400M) are not contractually locked and may flee if markets open weak. Deposit inflows (2.3B) are heavily weighted to wealth clients (70%), not institutional. SNB warned that absence of exit instructions is not confirmation of stability. AT1_rep called the structure 'a prayer not a legal defense' if Monday opens into panic. Sunday 06:00 bridge call scheduled but no binding contingency plan if Monday goes sideways.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB opened unlimited emergency liquidity facility but room immediately pivoted to UBS acquisition with 150B Confederation backstop—liquidity alone was never treated as sufficient, drove the acquisition structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution: room negotiated 50B UBS first-loss, 150B Confederation cap, AT1 subordination in deed, and Friday 19:30 announcement—this was the decision
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council 150B indemnification cap and SNB unlimited facility were non-negotiable closing conditions—UBS would not sign without them, Federal Council set hard cap, this shaped the deal structure
marker_evidence.client_flight: CS CEO reported outflows slowed at 16:45, then 2.3B inflows post-announcement; wealth_client demanded written deposit guarantee by 18:30 or would move assets Monday—client flight drove the Friday night timeline and guarantee language
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 subordination was embedded in section 3.2 of indemnification schedule as closing condition, fought over sequencing language ('absorbs losses first' vs 'junior to draw'), locked into deed—this was a binding constraint on the deal structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1_rep fought over subordination sequencing and warned of litigation risk, but room resolved it by locking 'AT1 absorbs first' language into deed—discussed extensively but did not block or reshape the final deal terms
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1_rep warned of court risk if subordination language was ambiguous, FINMA assured it holds legally, room locked language into deed—raised as risk and addressed, but did not force a concession or change the 150B cap or timeline
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: FINMA drew hard line: no announcement until documents filed by 18:30, forced Friday night signatures instead of Sunday—this dictated the timeline and drove the 19:30 announcement decision
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Multiple speakers warned Monday open is the real test, SNB said 'we've bought time not stability,' AT1_rep called it 'a prayer,' but room proceeded with Friday announcement and scheduled Sunday 06:00 bridge call—acknowledged but did not change the decision to announce Friday or add binding Monday contingencies
